title: Cells, tissues, shells, bones, leaves and flowers are shaped by the laws of physics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cells, tissues, shells, bones, leaves and flowers are shaped by the laws of physics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The material parts of living things (cells, tissues, shells, bones, leaves, flowers) are portions of matter whose particles have been moved, moulded and shaped in obedience to the laws of physics.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Cell and tissue, shell and bone, leaf and flower, are so many portions of matter, and it is in obedience to the laws of physics that their particles have been moved, moulded and conformed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter I, “Introductory”; topic “Organic form obeys physical law”. Scope: all organisms and their structural parts

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch01-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many local physical models can be tested with existing imaging and morphology, but no dataset matches the universal scope. The statement is also close to a general physical commitment, making decisive discrimination from rivals difficult.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For selected structures, fit physical models to measured material properties, forces, growth fields and resulting shapes, then compare predictions with observed morphogenesis. Agreement would support physical shaping in those cases, while systematic shape changes incompatible with the measured dynamics would refute the selected model but not the universal assertion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim ranges over all organisms and structural parts.

Observing compliance with physical law does not isolate which forces generated a form.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement is a universal programme for morphology rather than a relation between measured quantities. Morphometric archives contain shapes, not a variable called obedience to physical law. Because every finite set of forms is compatible both with the claim and with a rival that adds a non-physical cause, existing data do not discriminate it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No particular variable, law, or mismatch is named. Any measured shape can be read as obeying physics, and also as physics plus an unmeasured non-physical contribution, so there is no result that would confirm or refute the claim as stated.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Unexplained form can always be assigned either to unknown physics or to a vital residue.

The laws and the decision threshold are unspecified.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.1

discriminating power: 0.1
